boxes/what: A classifier says what is in a picture: a cat. To say where, draw the tightest rectangle around it. It is called a bounding box, since it bounds the object on every side.
boxes/axes: Measure in pixels, as an image does: x counts across from the left, and y counts down from the top.
boxes/tl: The top-left corner sits at one, one. Call it x one, y one.
boxes/br: The bottom-right corner, x two, y two, sits at five, four. Two corners, four numbers: the whole box.
boxes/width: Its width is right minus left: five minus one, four.
boxes/height: Its height is bottom minus top: four minus one, three.
boxes/guess: A network's guess, in blue, also covers twelve squares, but sits one down and one to the right.
boxes/ask: How well do the two agree? The goal is one number: one for a perfect match, and zero for a miss.
overlap/share: A first try: the area they share. It is a rectangle too, with edges taken from theirs.
overlap/lr: Its left edge is the larger left, two, and its right edge the smaller right, five: three wide.
overlap/tb: Its top is the larger top, two, and its bottom the smaller bottom, four: two tall.
overlap/inter: Three by two: six shared squares. That part is called the intersection, as where two roads intersect: the part in both.
overlap/apart: Slide the guess away, and the edges cross: right minus left is five minus six, minus one. A negative width means no overlap.
overlap/both: Miss both across and down, and both sides come out negative.
overlap/clamp: Multiplied, two negatives make a positive: an overlap that is not there. So each side is clamped at zero first, and the intersection is zero.
union/big: But shared area alone rewards a lazy guess: a box over the whole picture shares all twelve squares of the truth.
union/fair: So divide by everything either box covers. The huge box covers sixty squares: twelve over sixty, zero point two.
union/union: Everything either box covers is called the union: both boxes joined into one shape, not the rectangle around them.
union/count: For the first guess, twelve plus twelve counts the shared six twice, so take six off once: eighteen.
union/iou: Intersection over union, I O U for short: six over eighteen, about zero point three three.
union/range: Identical boxes score one, and boxes that do not touch score zero.
union/jaccard: The ratio is older than computers. In 1901, the Swiss botanist Paul Jaccard compared the plants of the Alps and the Jura this way: the species two places share, over the species found in either.
union/voc: For boxes, the yardstick is the Visual Object Classes challenge, a yearly contest described in 2010 by Mark Everingham and colleagues. A guess counted as correct only if its I O U was above a half.
union/low: They set that bar low on purpose, since even boxes drawn by people are not exact. The first guess, at zero point three three, falls short.
inside/nest: A box can lie wholly inside another. Box A is six by four: twenty four squares.
inside/small: Box B, inside it, is three by two: six.
inside/inter: Their overlap is all of B, and the union is just A: B adds nothing outside it.
inside/answer: So I O U is the small area over the big one: six over twenty four, zero point two five. Not a hit, though B lies inside A.
inside/rule: The other way round works too: a guess that holds the whole true box, with room to spare, scores the true box's area over its own.
